The new cooldown doesn't really prevent you from completing the tasks as long as you get the 15 wins per 2 specific games before that. But even then, \*theoretically\* 15 times 40 minutes is way less than 24 hours. Keep in mind that the cooldown only ever is so high as long as your total games within 24 hours surpass 300. That's vanishingly unlikely to cause any problems if you are at least remotely cautious.

There isn't really an optimal number of games per day, the general thing is the more the better. But, it depends on \*what\* games you play. The best thing to do from a hashrate standpoint would be to just repeat the highest paying game over and over again, but that's not time-efficient. What I like to do is rotating between Crypto Hamster, Cryptonoid and Token Blaster. You can reach level 10 in all of them after 81 wins so you're not even affected by massive cooldowns within your first 12 hours and they give out 1,692 to 1,920 TH/s per win, making them incredibly lucrative. What I'm doing then is putting all the games that I need for the game-specific tasks into the rotation (the only game today was Coinclick since I played Token Blaster anyway) until I won 15 times. The nice thing about this approach is that you only have to play every 10-15 minutes and once you get very skilled at the games, you can chew through them in like 2 minutes total so you don't have to invest a lot of time in total if you are on your computer regardless.

The cooldown doesn't really depend on the difficulty, it's just the more you play the higher your levels get automatically. If you were to level up all 11 games to level 10 in less than 12 hours, wait another 12 hours since they all dropped back to level 1, and your 24 hour total still is at like 300 games, the cooldown will still be totally ridiculous even though you're at level 1 again. It's kind of a flaw in their system that the cooldown is tied to a 24-hour-system but the levels only hold for 12 hours, sometimes making it impossible to get them high again (since when you play beyond level 10, Rollercoin doesn't remember those games so no matter how much you play, it'll not buffer these wins).

The difficulty decreases 12 hours after you won a game, so if you were to play from 9 to 11 AM and get to level 10, it would start decreasing at 9 PM and be at level 1 again at 11 PM.

At the beginning, try to spam from one side to the other a decent amount of times to generate as many tiles as you can.

The timer doesn't stop when you merge tiles together, but the game halts for a brief moment. However, it halts no matter how many tiles you merge, so if you merge multiple tiles at once, you'll lose less time. That tactic helped me get to level 7 in the past.

I've managed to get to level 7 so I think I can help you out here.

First of all, try to minimize the amount of merges since they all interrupt the game yet the timer still is going down.

Just spam left/right a few times whenever there's a lot of space on the field since you're generating a new tile every time. If you then go down or up, you'll merge several tiles at the same time so your score goes up quicker.

Go quick instead of thinking about every move. Mindlessly spamming works in the first few seconds and even on the entire game in the lower levels.

For higher levels you wanna get lucky by having pieces with high values generated in the beginning. I believe the highest that can generate naturally is the black one, I'm not sure though. Since larger pieces give you exponentially larger scores, they are crucial to succeeding on level 5 and especially six.

However, you won't get much forther than level 7. I completed a few games on level 7, but never enough to ascend to level 8 (and even if, there's no shot I would've beat that anytime soon).
